scope: post-activation SIGKILL and manual idle-state recovery on synthetic disposable Ubuntu host

fixture.kind: empty synthetic operator SQLite/config restore on disposable ext4 image

failure_injection.observation_capture: captured in a brain-owned lab text file before reset-failed; copied into root-owned evidence storage after recovery, so root-owned sealing did not precede the recovery action

recovery.verify_while_failed: rejected with attachment_root_action_failed; fail-closed but operator diagnostic is generic
recovery.operator_action: systemctl reset-failed on the exact disabled synthetic unit
recovery.finalize: passed only after systemd reported loaded, inactive, disabled, MainPID=0 and the idle database/inventory verified

interpretation: A post-activation SIGKILL did not trigger a systemd restart; attachment verification rejected the failed unit until an explicit reset-failed action.
After the unit became inactive and disabled, finalization verified and sealed the synthetic idle database and file inventory.
activated_stopped_idle_verified does not distinguish a clean stop from an abnormal process exit; this result proves post-exit idle state and inventory only.

This test began after activate had written both start-intent and the bound idle-probe receipt. A crash before idle-probe creation is a separate, unqualified failure window; create-only start intent prevents simply retrying that attachment.
limitations: The pre-reset systemd output was captured before reset but only sealed into root-owned storage afterward.
Only synthetic empty idle state was used; no production state or arbitrary restored database was tested.
No crash-consistency or durability claim is made for non-idle mutations, external side effects, or abrupt host power loss.
The generic attachment_root_action_failed diagnostic is safe but does not expose the underlying failed-unit state to the operator.
